context.body: Genesis through Deuteronomy distinguishes requests, responses, priestly formulas, intercession, restitution, pardon, retained consequence, and stated refusal to pardon. The bounded source is Exodus 32:30–35.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Moses asks whether Israel’s calf sin may be forgiven and offers his own erasure.
observations.label: Moses asks pardon after the calf: action

observations.body: the reply distinguishes the sinner, continued guidance, future punishment.
observations.label: Moses asks pardon after the calf: response

payload.posture: Read Exodus 32:30–35 as requests, law, and pardon evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The passage gives bounded Forgiveness evidence, but it does not make this request, response, condition, means, or outcome a universal procedure: Moses asks whether Israel’s calf sin may be forgiven and offers his own erasure, while the reply distinguishes the sinner, continued guidance, and future punishment.
payload.title: Moses asks pardon after the calf
